fixtures.name: ml_blog_intro
fixtures.task: Write the intro to my blog post announcing our new method for reducing classifier-free guidance saturation in diffusion models. Audience: ML practitioners.
fixtures.draft:
Classifier-free guidance (CFG) at high scales produces oversaturated colors, blown-out highlights, and a characteristic "cooked" look that most practitioners recognize immediately. The usual fix is to cap the guidance scale around 7–8, which trades off prompt adherence to keep images looking natural. But the saturation isn't fundamental to strong guidance — it's an artifact of how the guided score vector grows in magnitude as the scale increases, pushing samples outside the distribution the model was trained on.

We introduce a method that decouples guidance direction from guidance magnitude, letting you push prompt adherence to CFG scales of 15+ without the saturation collapse. The core idea: project the guidance update onto the tangent space of the predicted clean sample, then renormalize so the update's magnitude stays matched to the unconditional score. This preserves the directional information that makes CFG useful while preventing the norm inflation that causes saturation.

The rest of this post walks through the derivation, shows where standard CFG breaks down geometrically, and presents results on SD 1.5, SDXL, and Flux. FID and CLIP-score comparisons across guidance scales are in Table 1; qualitative side-by-sides are in Figure 3; ablations on the projection and renormalization steps are in Section 4.

fixtures.name: physics_abstract
fixtures.task: Draft an abstract for my paper reporting anomalous thermal conductivity measurements in twisted bilayer graphene at the magic angle.
fixtures.draft: We report thermal conductivity measurements of twisted bilayer graphene at twist angles spanning 0.9° to 1.3°, acquired via suspended microbridge thermometry between 20 K and 300 K. At the magic angle (1.08° ± 0.02°), the in-plane thermal conductivity is suppressed by a factor of 5.7 relative to Bernal-stacked bilayer graphene at 100 K, with the suppression persisting but weakening to a factor of 2.1 at 300 K. The phonon mean free path extracted from a Boltzmann transport analysis drops to 12 nm at the magic angle, compared to 240 nm at 1.3° twist. We attribute the suppression to hybridization between acoustic phonon modes and the flat-band-associated moiré phonon modes, which opens additional scattering channels with a characteristic energy scale of 4.2 meV consistent with the observed temperature dependence. The anomaly vanishes outside a narrow twist-angle window of ±0.05° around the magic angle, tracking the same angular sensitivity as the electronic flat bands.
